audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht’s International Business bachelor examines how firms operate across borders through management, marketing, finance, strategy and operations. This example follows the regular route.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR option combines business functions with leadership, entrepreneurship and data. The second examines how institutions and economic development shape business in emerging economies. Maastricht’s regular route includes a major, a study abroad semester and an individual thesis.

cellNotes.text: Both address how organisations function and are managed; Psychology of Organizations & Leadership approaches this through organisational behaviour, motivation, group dynamics, culture and leadership, rather than through management theory or organisational design.

Both address marketing management; Marketing & Consumer Engagement covers consumer behaviour, marketing strategy, digital marketing and brand strategy with marketing plans, without a cross-country focus.
Both address business strategy; Strategy & Digital Transformation has students develop a strategic plan from vision to execution, with a digital-technology emphasis.

Both develop leadership skills; Personal Leadership introduces transformational and authentic leadership with self-awareness and practical skills, which is the specific function of the Professional Development: Leadership Skills training, although it is a full course rather than a short training.
Both teach financial reporting; Accounting & Corporate Finance covers accounting theory and practice with emphasis on using and analysing financial statements and annual reports.
Both study financial markets, asset pricing, and risk and return. Maastricht also develops the corporate investment perspective.

Both give the economic foundations for business; Introduction to Economics covers micro- and macroeconomics, which is the economics part of Economics and Business, without the business-context applications.

Both address international business; International Business & Governance examines the institutional, political and cultural forces shaping global businesses, global trade and cross-border governance, which is the central subject of Global Business.
UCR takes a consumer product from needs to prototype and considers production scaling. Maastricht also develops quantitative methods for operations and supply decisions.
UCR develops database design, SQL and data management skills. Maastricht studies how organisations use information systems for business processes and strategy.

Both address starting and running a small venture; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations has teams develop a venture from idea to final pitch with market validation and business planning, without the small-business management content of the component.
Both use statistical inference and regression to analyse data. Maastricht’s skills course applies these methods to business case studies.
Choose a skills course from Maastricht’s approved fourth-semester list.
The regular route requires 26 EC of approved study abroad. Students need at least 53.5 EC from Year 1 to apply and all 60 EC before departure.

Choose two courses from one approved business major. Maastricht publishes options in accounting, finance, information management, supply chain management, marketing, organisation, strategy and entrepreneurship.
Take the second course from the same major. Maastricht specifies separate arrangements for some majors.
Choose one course from the approved quantitative economics, economics, ethics or law lists.
The 2.5 EC skills course prepares students for the individual thesis.
The required thesis is an individual academic research paper worth 8 EC.

notes.text: UCR offers courses in strategy, marketing, accounting, finance and entrepreneurship. Maastricht also requires dedicated work in supply chains, operations, management information systems and corporate governance, along with study abroad and an individual thesis.

The emerging economies option connects business with economic development, political institutions and sustainability. Maastricht’s formal Emerging Markets specialisation has a separate curriculum and an internship abroad.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENBUSI112.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
BENBUSI112.text: Accounting & Corporate Finance introduces financial and management accounting, financial-statement preparation and analysis, costing, pricing, budgeting and organisational control. Students assess investment decisions using accounting measures, discounted cash flow, net present value, internal rate of return and cost of capital. A case study examines the misuse of an accounting principle and its effects on financial statements.

source.reviewNote: Read the selected current profile in full; the summary represents accounting, control and investment-appraisal content proportionately, without claiming an entire advanced corporate-finance sequence.

BENBUSI211.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
BENBUSI211.text: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. Students study AI's capabilities and limits, applications across business functions and industries, and effects on labour markets, productivity, innovation and inequality. Business cases and scholarly arguments support analysis of governance, regulation and a country's AI readiness and industrial policy.

BENBUSI311.name: Transnational Business Law
BENBUSI311.text: Transnational Business Law studies legal frameworks for cross-border business, including contracts, trade, intellectual property, foreign investment and digital commerce. Comparative and international perspectives support analysis of legal risks through discussions, problem-based assignments and an arbitration simulation.

BENBUSI312.name: Money, Banking & Finance
BENBUSI312.text: Examines financial markets, commercial banks and central banks, including interest rates, financial regulation, financial crises and monetary policy. Students analyse financial problems and manage a simulated bank in the Stanford Banking Game, using Excel dashboards and financial forecasts to inform decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk.

This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.

BENECON211.text: Study the economy as a whole through topics such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment. Understand how governments and central banks use fiscal and monetary policies to influence economic performance over time. The course also explores business cycles, international trade, and economic crises, preparing students to evaluate policy debates and global economic trends.

BENECON311.text: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.

BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.text: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

BENENTR111.name: Consumer Product Design
BENENTR111.text: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.

BENENTR211.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement
BENENTR211.text: Marketing & Consumer Engagement examines consumer psychology, marketing strategy, responsible brand development and customer engagement. Students analyse a company strategy, design a brand and investigate a consumer phenomenon using academic literature and primary and secondary evidence. Digital marketing and customer-journey mapping connect analysis with practical recommendations.

BENENTR212.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation
BENENTR212.text: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.

BENENTR311.name: Market Research
BENENTR311.text: See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas—perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.

BENENTR312.name: International Business & Governance
BENENTR312.text: Examines how trade, globalisation and political, cultural and technological conditions shape international business decisions. Students analyse governance, responsibility and trade-policy conflicts, investigate a business question, and develop an evidence-based market-entry strategy. A tariff case applies game theory to stakeholder choices.

No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.text: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

BENLEAD111.text: Introduces self-leadership, leadership theory and emotional intelligence. Students use personality and emotional-intelligence profiles to reflect on group dynamics, study leadership cases, and develop a personal plan with practical goals. Assessment tools support educational reflection, with attention to differences in their scientific support.

BENLEAD211.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
BENLEAD211.text: Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership in diverse contexts, with particular attention to minority experiences. Students design and pilot a quantitative survey, collect data ethically, and use SPSS or RStudio for descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression. They interpret the findings and develop evidence-based leadership recommendations.

ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability
ENSDELT312.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.
